content.text: Overall, the 4 day retreat was a success, with positive feedback from all individuals. Many were happy with the presentations and felt the retreat supported their PhD programme progression. Others felt encouraged and supported by the School for putting together a research-focused retreat.

content.title: Faculty research retreat
content.author: ezekiel.kimeu
content.description: Faculty from all three campuses came together in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, for a 4-day retreat focused on faculty development in academia and research. The first day began with a general introduction and welcome remarks from the Dean, Professor Sharon Brownie. Guests from various AKU entities were in attendance to discuss topics including enhancing capacity in teaching and learning, library support for faculty research, faculty key performance indicators and alumni engagement. Visiting faculty from other universities volunteered to meet with SONAM-EA faculty to provide support for research and PhD progression. Currently, the School has seven faculty enrolled at Stellenbosch University and six at the University of South Africa (UNiSA). Janet Bell from Stellenbosch University, along with Gloria Tshweneagae and Gisela van Rensburg from UNiSA met with their respective students to discuss research proposals and evaluate PhD progression. Non PhD faculty met with Rachel Rossiter from Charles Sturt University, Australia and Eleanor Holroyd from Auckland University of Technology, New Zealand. These sessions covered research merit, developing a research question and mixed methods research. The retreat also provided faculty with the opportunity to participate in different research-focused sessions of their choice. Sessions were led by visiting faculty and covered topics such as the concept of 'doctorateness', conceptual versus theoretical frameworks, writing chapters, conducting literature reviews, writing for publication, choosing a journal, and standards for reporting qualitative research. In addition, Charles Docherty, Director of the Centre for Innovation in Medical Education, AKU-Karachi, presented a session on clinical simulation to conduct research and evaluate existing practice. On the final day, Dawn Kuzemski, Assistant Director of Nursing at Abu Dhabi Health Services, discussed the different roles of a preceptor, benefits and challenges of preceptorship and how to prepare a preceptor workshop. Participating faculty were engaged in learning activities throughout the presentation. One activity focused on role play, in which one faculty member played the preceptor and another played a student reporting to the preceptor on a patient's status. This provided opportunity for faculty to improve communication skills, with a specific focus on how to teach, reinforce and correct mistakes.
